rows.question: Explain DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP and latency in approximately 500 words.

result.answer:
DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP, and latency are fundamental components that work together to enable seamless communication over the internet. Each plays a distinct yet interconnected role in how data is accessed, transmitted, and secured between devices worldwide.

Domain Name System (DNS) acts as the internet’s phonebook. When you type a website address like www.example.com into your browser, DNS translates this human-readable domain name into an IP address—a numerical identifier that locates the server hosting the site. This translation process is essential because computers do not understand domain names; they only recognize IP addresses. Without DNS, users would need to remember complex sequences of numbers instead of simple web addresses.

Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) governs how data is transferred across networks. It ensures reliable delivery by breaking large files into smaller packets, numbering them, and sending them in sequence. If any packet arrives out of order or is lost, TCP detects the error and requests retransmission until all data reaches its destination intact. This protocol also manages flow control and congestion to prevent overwhelming network resources.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) provides encryption and authentication for secure communication. When a user visits a website using HTTPS, TLS establishes an encrypted channel between the browser and the server. It verifies the identity of the site through digital certificates, encrypts data in transit, and protects against eavesdropping or tampering. This security layer is critical for protecting sensitive information such as passwords, credit card details, and personal data.

Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) defines how messages are formatted and transmitted between web browsers and servers. It allows clients to request web pages and servers to respond with content like HTML documents. While HTTP operates over TCP, it lacks built-in security features. Its secure counterpart, HTTPS, integrates TLS to protect data during transmission.

Latency refers to the time delay between a user’s action—such as clicking a link—and the response received. It includes processing delays on devices and networks, routing times across servers, and transmission speeds. High latency can cause sluggish performance in applications like video calls or online gaming, while low latency ensures responsiveness and real-time interaction.

Together, these protocols form the backbone of internet functionality. DNS enables easy access to websites; TCP ensures data integrity during transfer; TLS secures sensitive exchanges; HTTP facilitates content delivery; and latency determines user experience quality. Understanding their roles helps users appreciate how complex yet efficient internet communication truly is. Each component contributes uniquely to the overall performance, reliability, and security of online interactions. While they operate behind the scenes, their synergy underpins nearly every digital activity today.
Note: This is general model knowledge and is not verified by the PSU Esports Studio - Phuket knowledge base.

rows.question: Compare TCP and UDP, including one advantage and one disadvantage of each.

result.answer:
TCP: Pros: Ensures reliable data delivery through acknowledgments and retransmissions. Cons: Introduces latency due to overhead from connection setup and error checking.  
UDP: Pros: Offers low latency with minimal overhead for real-time applications. Cons: Does not guarantee delivery or order of packets, making it unreliable for critical data transmission.
